chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding inheritance: that which Islam acquired from the wealth of a polytheist which had not yet been divided, the women have their shares from it.

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ الْإِسْلَامَ: acquired by Islam / taken by Muslims

ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's ruling on the distribution of undivided wealth from polytheists regarding women's shares?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that undistributed wealth acquired from polytheists (māl al-mushrikīn) remains subject to standard inheritance laws, specifically granting women their prescribed shares. This ruling highlights the continuity of Quranic inheritance principles even in the context of early Islamic fiscal acquisitions (ghanimah/fay'), distinguishing it from the unique distribution rules of the Prophet's time. It underscores the scholarly view that women's financial rights were integral to the early Muslim community's economic structure.
